messages:
maria: FYI ran a bunch of profiling after the recent weight-only AWQ packing change — seeing a ~12% tail p99 latency regression on long context workloads with KV cache enabled. :frowning:

jing: ugh. do you have the flamegraph or perf counters? was it on the same kernel routing commit?

maria: yes same commit. quick paste from the runtime sampler (4k ctx, warm cache):\n\n```
hotspots (samples):
  matmul_fp16_kernel       42%
  kv_pack_unpack_path     18%  <-- surprising
  kv_cache_lookup         12%
  attention_kv_ops         9%
  scheduler_overhead       6%
  memcpy                  13%
```

maria: packing/unpacking shows up much higher than before. packaging overhead seems correlated with group-size=64 AWQ quant layout. link to trace: https://perf.redwood/internal/trace/1769001234

zach: can you repro with group-size=32 and group-size=128? packing algorithm complexity changes with group size so overhead can jump nonlinearly.

maria: ran quick A/B: group=32 -> pack down to 9% samples, group=64 -> 18%, group=128 -> 15%. so 64 is the worst here.

jing: interesting. group=64 likely triggers a codepath that uses the byte-aligned packer that then forces extra memcpy rounds for KV streaming. try `AWQ_PACKER=streaming` vs `AWQ_PACKER=batch` env var.

maria: tried `streaming` -> pack cost halved but matmul perf regressed slightly (maybe because kernel chooser falls back to scalar path). results: pack 9% -> matmul 44% (vs 42% baseline) but end-to-end p99 improved by ~4%.

raquel: I saw similar on dedicated infra last week. the kernel selector uses heuristics on sequence length and group size; when packer changes shard alignment the vectorized unpack path becomes inapplicable and we hit scalar fallback. I'll open an opt-change PR to relax the threshold. @jing can you add a unit to ensure pack alignment keeps vector path available?

jing: yes, I'll add a small alignment shim and a unit test that validates `unpack_vectorized` is chosen for group sizes we expect.

zach: also check batching heuristics — small micro-batches with KV cache hits cause more frequent pack/unpack operations. if the batching window is too tight we pay pack overhead more often. try increasing the `max_batch_delay_ms` for long-ctx routes.

maria: yep, when I increased max_batch_delay from 10ms to 30ms median latency rose a little but p99 improved. tradeoff looks reasonable for interactive LLMs with long contexts.

perf-bot: regression-detect: alert for commit sha abcdef1 — +11.7% p99 on long-context test-suite. See: https://perf.redwood/reports/regressions/abcdef1

raquel: timeline: can we canary the alignment shim + packer fallback in a small Dedicated pool? If it fixes vector path, pack overhead should drop without changing quant layout.

maria: plan: 1) add alignment shim (jing) 2) tune kernel selector thresholds (raquel) 3) run canary on dedicated pool with group=64 traces + long ctx perf harness 4) if green roll to hosted. I'll create a tracking issue and throw the perf logs there.

maria: created issue: https://go.redwood/issue/INT8-613 — details and raw traces attached. tagging perf team. :thumbsup:

zach: one more note — verify KV cache hit rate instrumentation; in a few traces we saw false misses due to metadata mismatch after packing. that amplifies pack cost reporting. check `kv_cache_key_v2` schema.

jing: good catch. I'll add extra assertions in the packer to avoid key-level canonicalization regressions.

raquel: if anyone's free later let's do a quick pairing session to run the bisect and pin the exact commit that changed pack layout. :eyes:

maria: thanks all, will update the issue with canary results once the alignment shim lands. :pray:
